message.content:
**Decision: Buy — order filled.**

I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and found a fundamentally strengthening business despite a headline dip in earnings. Total net sales rose 2% to $391.0 billion, led by Services up 13% to $96.2 billion (a 73.9% gross-margin segment) and total gross margin expanding to 46.2% from 44.1%. Operating income grew 6% to $123.2 billion, and operating cash flow was a robust $118.3 billion. Net income fell to $93.7 billion and diluted EPS to $6.08 (from $6.13) solely because of a one-time, non-operational $10.2 billion net income tax charge tied to the European Court of Justice's September 2024 State Aid ruling — underlying profitability actually improved. The balance sheet remains fortress-like: $140.8 billion of cash and marketable securities and $95.0 billion returned to shareholders via buybacks plus $15.2 billion of dividends in FY2024. Risks I weighed were real but manageable — Greater China net sales declined 8% to $67.0 billion, iPhone sales were flat at $201.2 billion, and the DOJ antitrust suit and EU DMA investigations could impose fines or business-practice changes. On balance, a 2.0x revenue multiple on a business with these margins and cash generation is attractive, so I placed one buy order: 22 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.72, which filled at that price (quote was $222.68 bid / $222.72 ask, last $222.70), for a total of $4,899.84 — well inside the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps, funded entirely from the $50,000 of existing cash with no money moved out of the account, and leaving the existing 100 MSFT shares untouched.
